reviews.body:
Reviewed head `e9df5cb`. Merging is harmless (nothing calls it), but I recommend **not wiring it into the demo screens**. No case was found where stale data is shown as current: every failure goes the safe way, but fresh data becomes `unknown`, so a working phone would look broken on stage. Each finding was reproduced with a probe.

**Findings** (`src/monitoring-state/project.mjs`)
1. **High — `:152`:** a phone clock 300 ms ahead of the server makes a point permanently `unknown` (`source-after-server-receipt`). The backend accepts captures up to 30 s ahead and clamps age to 0, so it reports the same point as `fresh`.
2. **High — `:160`:** setting `timeUncertaintyMs` to absorb skew backfires: any point younger than the uncertainty gets a negative minimum age and becomes `unknown` (30 s uncertainty → a 5 s-old point is `unknown`).
3. **High — `:101-106`:** with a history, any other point within 2× uncertainty of the latest makes location `unknown` (3 s cadence + 2 s uncertainty → `unknown` forever); one old point with `null` uncertainty blocks every later point for the trip.
4. **High — `:204-206`:** on the contact screen the driver's permission is unknowable; passing `unknown` forces `location.status='unknown'` even when the fact is `recent`.
5. Medium — `:6`, `:221`: raw backend job statuses (`pending`, `claimed`, `authorized`, `rejected`, `unknown`, `unavailable`) throw a TypeError for the whole projection, hiding location too; omitting `timeUncertaintyMs` (`:57`) or using the backend's `accuracy` field name (`:197`) also throws.
6. Low — `:119/135`: after the phone sleeps, `performance.now()` pauses while wall time advances, so the first tick after resume is all `unknown`.

**Integration:** only location can be fed today, and it re-derives what `GET /v1/trips/:id/snapshot` already returns (`freshness`, `ageMs`). Responses, deadlines, notification states and coverage have no backend read endpoint yet. The backend will add `GET /v1/trips/:id/status` (trip, open security check, incident, per-channel delivery status, location freshness) for both screens. The one useful extra here, ageing between polls, is one line: `ageMs + (performance.now() - tReceived)`.

Recommendation for tomorrow: drive the Active Trip and contact screens from `/status` and `/snapshot` directly and park this module.

Tests: `node --test tests/monitoring-state/*.test.mjs` → **51 passed** (Node 26.8.1; README asks for 22.22.3).

_Review prepared with Claude Code (AI-assisted, read-only verification in a scratch worktree) and posted by @Robertzu43._

reviews.author: Robertzu43
reviews.body:
> Written by Robert's review agent (Claude), posted from @Robertzu43 at Robert's direction. Reviewed head: `e9df5cb`.

**Verdict: request changes. I recommend closing this PR.**

**Utility:** The backend already serves the contact snapshot with freshness and age. `GET /v1/contact/trips/:id/location` returns `{ location: {capturedAt, receivedAt, latitude, longitude, accuracy}, freshness: 'fresh'|'stale'|'unavailable', ageMs, readAt }` (`codex/aws-durable-backend`, `src/location/routes.ts:32–34`). The #22 contact map can render that and age it locally between polls. This 234-line client-side reprojection of server history duplicates the server's authority and, as the findings below show, hides real locations on realistic input.

### Blockers (reproduced by the review scripts on `e9df5cb`; the suite passes 51/51)

1. **`src/monitoring-state/project.mjs:101`** A realistic 1 Hz location stream in one session with `timeUncertaintyMs: 500` leaves `location.lastKnown` **always null** (`latest-source-time-uncertain`). Selection ignores same-session sequence order.
2. **`:201`** An unusable point that is newer or overlapping replaces the usable selection, so the stale usable location disappears. That contradicts the PR's own test "unusable latest positions do not hide a stale usable location".
3. **`:77`** Duplicates are matched on raw JSON, including `receivedAt`. A harmless retried upload, or `…58.000Z` vs `…58Z`, becomes a conflict and erases the driver's latest report.
4. **`:96`** A single conflicting pair anywhere in history, such as one cached GPS fix with an older `sourceAt`, sets `lastKnown` to null for the rest of the trip.
5. **`tests/monitoring-state/fault-matrix.test.mjs:28`** The false-freshness matrix proves nothing. The base facts are already 602 s old against a 10 s budget, so all 80 combinations still pass with the clock, session and disagreement checks deleted.

### If it is kept anyway

- **`:214`** The deadline comparison is gated on the agreement record's freshness, which the README says it is independent of.
- **`:160`** `event-in-server-future` is reported from uncertainty alone, so freshly received reports are always `unknown`.
- **`:163`** A stale but valid server anchor turns definitely-stale facts and definitely-reached deadlines into `unknown`.
- **`:186`** Gaps are deduplicated on exact JSON, so an open and a closed version of the same gap both survive and block every later fact.
- **`:224`** Notifications are split before `select()`, which hides conflicts where the same event ID appears on two messages.
- **`:209`** One bad deadline revision throws for the whole projection.
- **`:202`** Rejected points are counted twice in `evidence`.
- **`:147`** Unknown facts can come back with empty `reasons`.
- **`:90`** `select()` is O(n²) and re-parses timestamps for every pair, which means millions of regex parses per tick on hours of 1 Hz data.
